widgets_values:
@film is a real frame of the film this shot belongs to. Match its realism exactly: same camera, same lens, same daylight, same colour, same grain. Another frame shot the same day at the same river.

A VERY WIDE LANDSCAPE SHOT OF A BIG RIVER. The camera is FAR OUT over the middle of a wide river, high above the water, looking across at the far bank in the distance. This is a distant landscape view, not a shot of people: the people are incidental specks in it.

COMPOSITION: the river fills the LOWER HALF of the frame — deep, opaque, dark brown-green water in huge volume, running left to right, standing waves and white rapids, spray, no rocks and nothing to stand on, no near bank. Across the MIDDLE of the frame, far away, a thin horizontal band: the far bank's grassy lip and a narrow strip of clearing. Above it a TALL WALL OF RAINFOREST filling the upper third — big trees towering over the bank — and a little pale sky.

THE THREE MEN ARE TINY, DISTANT FIGURES on that far bank, standing still and facing the camera across the water. Each man is only ONE SEVENTEENTH of the frame height: much shorter than the grass clumps beside them, dwarfed by the trees behind them, no larger than a fingertip held at arm's length. Their faces and hands are not resolvable at all — they read only as three small coloured shapes. THEY MUST BE TINY. Do not bring the camera closer to them and do not enlarge them.

Their order and heights: on the LEFT @explorer, the TALLEST, a maroon-red cap and dark doublet over maroon breeches. In the MIDDLE @guide, the SHORTEST, bare-chested with a pale cream wrap. BEHIND and slightly RIGHT of them, set further back, @soldier, height between the two, a tall dark hat and a rust-brown coat. Hands empty.

No haze, no mist, no god rays, no sun shafts. Plain hard tropical daylight like @film. No text, no border, no letterbox bars.

nodes.title: PROMPT · v02 (1203 chars · verbatim from the prompt embedded in the landed MP4)
widgets_values:
ONE UNBROKEN LIVE-ACTION TAKE. NO FADE, NO DISSOLVE, NO CROSS-FADE, NO BLENDING OF TWO PICTURES, NO GHOSTING, NO SOFTENING, NO CUT. Every frame is a sharp, fully detailed photograph of the same place.

The camera is on a crane pulling BACKWARDS over the river, already moving on the first frame and still moving on the last, at one steady speed. It travels in a straight line, back and gently up. The whole change of size comes from that physical travel: real parallax, near grass sliding past faster than the far trees. No zoom.

As the camera retreats: the two men keep walking toward it out of the tall grass and steadily become smaller in frame. A third man in a tall dark hat and rust-brown coat steps out of the grass behind them and follows, staying behind them. The grassy lip of the bank drops into the bottom of frame and dark fast river water appears below it, growing until it fills the lower half of the frame — deep water running left to right, standing waves, white rapids. The three men reach the edge of the bank and stop, standing still and facing the camera across the water.

Same hard tropical daylight, same colour, same grain and same lens for all ten seconds. No text, no border.

nodes.title: HANDOFF · READ FIRST · for Brynley
widgets_values:
# HANDOFF — cgi-042 — plug downstream work in HERE

Everything left of this frame is the **historical chain** that produced the approved output(s): BUILT - NOT RUN,
every provider node **BYPASSED** (purple) so Queue cannot spend. Do not rewire it; branch from the handoff nodes.

**Per approved video:** `LoadVideo (APPROVED)` → `GetVideoComponents` → `images` (float32 RGB, full frame range),
`fps`, `bit_depth`, `color_space`. Three labelled slots follow for your passes, in order:
**16-bit colour conversion → depth pass → stereo 3D conversion.**

**COLOUR — read before converting.** The note beside each handoff states the file's MEASURED container tags.
Comfy decodes 10-bit sources to 32-bit float (no 8-bit truncation), but an **untagged** file is labelled
`color_space = "sRGB"` by `GetVideoComponents` as a fallback, and its YUV→RGB matrix is the decoder default.
For untagged files the true matrix is **UNVERIFIED** — declare it explicitly in your conversion; do not trust
the reported "sRGB". Tagged files (bt709) are safe to take at their tag.

**Frame rate.** Generated takes are 24.000 fps; the film is 23.976. Conform frame-for-frame (relabel), not by
retiming, unless editorial says otherwise.

nodes.title: v03 STEREO chain — EXR → fal depth x241 → median5 + atadenoise → mesh comp → eyes → spatial
widgets_values:
Same chain as v02, same parameters — only the picture changed.

`v03-frames-png`/`v03-exr` (241 half-float) → `fal-ai/image-preprocessors/depth-anything/v2` x241 via fireAndLog, $0.2410 (+4 gap retries, ledgered) → `v03-depth` → per-pixel **temporal median(5)** (`depth-median5.py`) → **atadenoise s=9:0a=0.06:0b=0.3** → `v03-depth-median5-smoothed` → `stereo-render.py` mesh comp (2.08M verts, displace 0.346, sep 0.064, conv/z 4.82, AoV 19.264, scale 3.80) in Resolve `cgi-042-stereo-pipe2` → 241 SBS @ 7680x2160, **0 px borders** → eye split ProRes HQ → `spatial make` (cdist 65, hfov 90, rect, primary L).

Adjacent-frame jitter (8-bit levels): raw 4.13/15.63 → median5 1.33/6.50 → smoothed **0.90/4.82**. Rougher water than v02 (which was secretly the calm plate) makes v03 depth noisier; residual step at f72→73 (~11.9, water-region reassignment) is FLAGGED to Brynley for hand-painted stabilisation — see `_handoff/cgi-042-stereo-v03-2026-09-30/`.

Outcrop drift in last ~2 s is generative (i2v invention), **accepted by Kyle — not a stereo defect**.

nodes.title: PROMPT · char-a sheet v04 (2835 chars · verbatim from sidecar)
widgets_values: The reference images are frames of one actor from a documentary re-enactment: a European explorer of about 1537 with a soft maroon-red cloth cap with a small soft brim, long dark wavy hair to the shoulders, a full dark beard, a grey-mauve quilted doublet belted at the waist, FULL MAROON BREECHES THAT REACH DOWN TO THE KNEE, pale cream mud-stained hose below them, tall brown leather boots with folded-over tops, WHITE SHIRT CUFFS showing at both wrists, and on the front of his belt a BROAD FLAT PALE-STEEL BLADE hung beside a large plain bright metal ring, with a BRIGHT RED POUCH next to it. Make ONE character reference sheet of this man. ONE THING CHANGES FROM THE PREVIOUS SHEET AND EVERYTHING ELSE STAYS. THE MAROON LOWER GARMENT IS A SMOOTH KNEE-LENGTH SKIRT, NOT BREECHES. It hangs straight and flat with a soft A-line and has NO SEPARATION BETWEEN THE LEGS — no inner-leg seam, no split, no gathered or paned or blousy breeches — and its HEM SITS ABOVE THE KNEE. Below the hem, pale cream mud-stained hose, wound and wrapped. This is read off frames 260.600 and 252.500, where no inner-leg line is visible at any magnification. KEEP EXACTLY AS THEY WERE: the soft maroon cap with the downturned brim, the long dark wavy shoulder-length hair, the full dark beard, the grey-mauve quilted doublet with its short flared skirt and white shirt cuffs at both wrists, the broad dark belt with its large plain metal ring, the broad flat pale-steel blade hanging bare over the front, the bright red pouch, and the tall brown boots with folded-over tops. The full-figure profile (259.500) is the identity and proportion anchor. The lower garment is the ONE thing being corrected — build it from 260.600 and 252.500, and do not invent a leg split that the film does not show. Every view must be the SAME man as in the reference images — same face, same age, same skin tone, same hair, same build, same garments, same colours. Do not idealise, do not restyle, do not modernise. Add NOTHING that is not visible in the references: no jewellery, no body paint, no headband, no weapons or props that are not in the frames. Lay it out as a character reference sheet on one neutral mid-grey seamless background under even soft studio light (no jungle, no sunlight, no shadows on the ground). Top row: three head-and-shoulders portraits at the same scale — facing camera, three-quarter, and true profile — eye-line level, neutral expression. Below: a full-body front view and a full-body back view standing straight, feet visible. Along one edge, small detail insets of the hands and of each garment and carried object, close enough to read fabric, stitching and wear. Photoreal, sharp, natural skin texture, no painterly or illustrated look. 3:2 frame. No text anywhere: no labels, no letters, no numbers, no arrows, no captions, no watermark.

widgets_values: The reference images are frames of one actor from a documentary re-enactment: an indigenous Panamanian guide — a LEAN, WIRY, YOUNG man — natural rather than trained, with visible pectoral and shoulder shape but a SMOOTH STOMACH and no defined abdominal muscles: bare chest and arms, warm brown skin, dark straight BLUNT BOB-CUT hair with a fringe, the hair ending AT THE NAPE OF THE NECK and well above the shoulders, no beard, a DIRTY GREY-BROWN cloth, mud-stained from the hem upward and visibly worn, WRAPPED round the waist and hanging straight and flat to mid-thigh with a FOLDED-OVER TOP EDGE at the waist and a vertical overlap at the side, barefoot, carrying a plain steel machete with a wooden grip in one hand. Make ONE character reference sheet of this man. TWO THINGS CHANGE FROM THE PREVIOUS SHEET. (1) THE PHYSIQUE WAS OVER-CORRECTED INTO A GYM BODY. The previous sheet drew a defined six-pack and deep serratus. On frames 253.500 and 255.500 he is LEAN AND WIRY with visible pectoral and shoulder shape and a SMOOTH ABDOMEN — no six-pack, no visible abdominal separations, no serratus definition. Natural, not trained. (2) THE CLOTH IS NOT NEW. The previous sheet drew clean new cream linen. The film's wrap is DIRTY: grey-brown, MUD-STAINED FROM THE HEM UPWARD, worn and used. KEEP: the bare chest, the warm brown skin, the straight blunt bob ending at the nape well above the shoulders, the straight fringe, the flat wrapped construction with its folded-over top edge and side overlap, the bare feet, and the machete. The two in-shot frontals (253.500, 255.500) carry the build, and they are the reason this sheet is being redrawn. The back view (258.100) is the hair length and the wrap's construction. nodes.title: PROMPT · char-c sheet v04 (3248 chars · verbatim from sidecar)
widgets_values: The reference images are frames of one actor from a documentary re-enactment: a European soldier of a Spanish survey party of about 1537: a DARK NEAR-BLACK SOFT HAT whose crown is built of thick vertical ribs and whose broad stiff brim is turned DOWN all round, and whose crown is a MODERATELY TALL RIBBED DRUM — about four fifths as tall as the crown itself is WIDE, standing well clear of the head; DARK HAIR IN LOOSE ROPEY MATTED LOCKS THAT END AT THE JAW, and a full dark beard and moustache; a plain SATURATED BURNT-ORANGE long-sleeved coat reaching to mid-thigh with a slightly flared skirt AND A COMPLETELY PLAIN FRONT WITH NO BUTTONS OF ANY KIND; a narrow pale grey-blue cloth sash tied round the waist with its end hanging; white shirt cuffs at the wrists; a large plain metal ring on the belt at the front and a pale bone-cream sheath hanging at the left hip; pale cream hose stained with mud, tucked into tall dark brown leather boots with folded-over tops. Make ONE character reference sheet of this man. ONE THING CHANGES FROM THE PREVIOUS SHEET AND EVERYTHING ELSE STAYS. THE COAT SKIRT CARRIES EVENLY SPACED PALE GOLD-CREAM VERTICAL STRIPS running the FULL DEPTH of the skirt, all the way round. Draw them as VERTICAL SLASHES IN THE ORANGE CLOTH SHOWING A PALE GOLD-CREAM LINING BEHIND — regular, evenly spaced, the full height of the skirt from the sash to the hem. KEEP EXACTLY AS IT WAS: the dark near-black soft hat with its thick vertical ribs, its moderately tall drum crown and its stiff downturned brim; the dark hair in loose ropey matted locks ENDING AT THE JAW; the full dark beard; the saturated burnt-orange coat to mid-thigh with a COMPLETELY PLAIN FRONT AND NO BUTTONS; the pale grey-blue sash; the white shirt cuffs; the metal ring at the belt front and the bone-cream sheath at the left hip; the mud-stained hose and the tall dark brown boots. AND STILL: no helmet, no morion, no steel cap, no crest, comb or feather, no breastplate, no armour, NO SWORD. The whole-figure crop (c3-alone-259.500) carries the coat skirt at its largest. The strips are the ONE thing being added; everything else on the previous sheet was signed as a match and must not move. Every view must be the SAME man as in the reference images — same face, same age, same skin tone, same hair, same build, same garments, same colours. Do not idealise, do not restyle, do not modernise. Add NOTHING that is not visible in the references: no jewellery, no body paint, no headband, no weapons or props that are not in the frames. Lay it out as a character reference sheet on one neutral mid-grey seamless background under even soft studio light (no jungle, no sunlight, no shadows on the ground). Top row: three head-and-shoulders portraits at the same scale — facing camera, three-quarter, and true profile — eye-line level, neutral expression. Below: a full-body front view and a full-body back view standing straight, feet visible. Along one edge, small detail insets of the hands and of each garment and carried object, close enough to read fabric, stitching and wear. Photoreal, sharp, natural skin texture, no painterly or illustrated look. 3:2 frame. No text anywhere: no labels, no letters, no numbers, no arrows, no captions, no watermark.
